Hello my fellow parents! Have any of you done taking cara babies sleep training? Our former amazing / independent sleeper has majorly regressed at 19 months after about a month of back to back sicknesses and co-sleeping.  My husband and I are desperate for her to get back to where she was and I've heard good things about this program. Any and all tips would be greatly appreciated. :pray::skin-tone-2:
I'd actually recommend the sleep module by Big Little Feelings.  Worked within 2-3 days for both my boys when they regressed

I've *just started* the "Fuss It Out" method from "My Precious Little Sleep" with my 5mo.

It's been 3 nights so far, we are seeing some improvements for sure (was waking ~5 times last week, now 2x)

our pediatrician recommended taking cara babies, but graduated extinction worked best for us.

hang in there; it does get better :two_hearts:
I've not heard about taking cara babies, will definitely look it up :relaxed:

We used Taking Cara Babies and it worked; however, we did modify the program a bit. We also worked through some of the program from Big Little Feelings, and it was very similar, but a little "chiller". Cara can be... intense :sweat_smile:

We decided on the FIO (Fuss it Out) because our little dude does *not* calm himself when we hold him easily (sometimes takes more than 10 minutes, he gets even angrier somehow, and we end up needing to walk through the house, with lights on, etc.).

So pickup/put down methods didn't look very promising.

First night was tough, but got significantly better the next day
This is so helpful thank you all!!
Is that an MLS official ball? If yes, I have one of those too and my kids love it

I believe @user mentioned he used it! I personally used extinction (or FIO) with my little one and it worked well for us, but she hasn’t had any sleep regressions yet (currently 6 months) so haven’t had to put it to the test too much

@user I took the taking Cara babies courses in the beginning and didnt follow it exactly, but it was helpful! I was actually thinking of doing it again because our little guy is in a regression right now. So let me know if you do it!

We purchased taking cara babies yesterday and watched about 10 or so videos last night so were ready to take action!  :muscle::skin-tone-2: Little lady woke up 1 time in the middle of the night and we waited 5 mins before checking on her, went in told her we loved her and it's time to go to bed, etc, she went back to sleep 5 mins after that on her own, and then woke up for the day at 6:15!! Teething gels are awesome. Swaddles are awesome. Tummy time is awesome. Skin to skin is awesome (both parents).

Pacifiers don't always work. Some babies don't like them. If yours does, great! Others prefer swaddling. Others want to be held. Pay attention, baby will show you.

Best baby formula for us was Kendamil, especially the goat infant formula. But they're all great. I don’t know why other brands didn't sit well at all. Expensive but was worth it. Don't feel guilty about any biological challenges with milk/latching. Formula babies are fine and healthy, no shame. Do your best and focus on loving your little one.

Get all the help you can get. Never feel guilty about it. 

Perfection is the enemy of good. Go with the flow as much as possible. Let the baby drive first 3 months, you will slowly gain control after. This time is about connection, not routines; those come naturally.

What works for other babies might not work for yours. Study your baby, like a puzzle to solve. It's so fun when you crack their code. 

Don't forget yourself, well-being, etc. Ask for help, for breaks, for sushi, whatever you need. Spoil yourself whenever you get a chance.

Enjoy the ride. Praise God if you're religious. Best wishes and may it be a healthy journey

9 months PP and still going through all the things - so here's my brain dump :joy:

The highs and lows of early postpartum absolutley rocked me to my core - you hear about it before it happens to you, but you truly dont know until you know:joy:! Those nights where you are like 'how am i going to get through this' will quickly be forgotten and the next day can be replaced with 'there is no better feeling than this'

Lean on other moms for solidarity. It helps so much knowing you are not alone in what you are going through. share the highs and the lows!

Cluster feeding - WTF:joy: they go through phases where they feed allllll the time when they are newborns. whether BF or bottle, just hunker down on the couch with TV and snacks and a full water bottle.

You will never look at a mom with kids out in public the same :joy: I used to glance past families with multiple small kids in public. Now my internal talk track is "i hope that mom is doing ok, does she need any help ? does she know she is doing a great job? is she thriving or surviving?"

In the beginning, dont want money on 'cute outfits'. they live in double zip jammies and onesies. whatever is easiest to change diapers. they dont need jeans and shoes :joy: Also Buy clothes like 6 months in advance when they are on clearance. aint nobody need to be paying more than $15 for a onesie they are going to poop in.

Comparison is the thief of joy. All babies are on their own timelines and there is so much that impacts everything from sleep to eating to milestones. Try not to compare your baby/experience against others because as everyone has said above, every baby is different. As soon as you accept that, things will feel so much better and you can just try to enjoy the current phase youre in, even if its a hard one.

Dont drive yourself insane with schedules in the beginning. Besides feeding ~every 3 hours or on demand, pay attention to suggested wake windows/cues instead of trying to put them on a strict schedule. I drove myself nuts trying to fit my baby into a rigid Moms on Call schedule in the beginning but when they wake up early fro ma nap (or dont nap:joy:) or feed outside the scheduled time it drove me nuts. as soon as i let go of the control and let my baby lead the way, while just trying my best to meet their needs, things got so much more enjoyable :heart:

*Kids vs AI*

As the dad of a 6 and 2 year old, I like many parents am often sensitive or unsure on the appropriate amount of exposure to screens and tech, particularly as an early-millennial who had a mostly tech-free childhood (the first UK iPhone launched when I left uni in 2007....).

Anyway, with AI it feels like exposing the children to some form of it early will benefit them long-term, they will use it obviously in ways we probably can't imagine. Inspired by recent AI hackathon activities at Carta, I gave my 6 year old her first 'AI-enablement', allowing her to create a game on Google Canvas. It was wonderful to see how she could take her creative ideas, voice them into Google and enjoy the fruit of her creations. While under my guidance her first game was not the most edifying ('FruitMerge' - a game where you drop one fruit on to another, resulting in a different fruit being created.....), as I left her to her own devices she created more constructive games for herself. The wonderful culmination is, after I left her for 5 minutes alone, she had fully commanded Canvas to create her own spelling game for herself :face_holding_back_tears:. Whilst tech can obviously negative influences, this was a wonderful example to see how AI can be an enabling superpower for children (believe our very own investor Marc Andreesen said something recently about how AI can be a great enabler / tutor for children).
you must be SO proud!
This is awesome. As a parent who has been turned onto Fruit Merge from her children, I would much rather have them play Spelling Master!

Another AI exposure to share - we've started bringing blank sketchpads out with us and having our sons create something from their imagination. We then take a picture of their drawing and have them describe it so ChatGPT can turn it into a cartoon version. Example below. They love it!

My 13 year old nephew is a thoughtful young person - really personally torn between phone and friend - and when I showed him how we could brainstorm with Canvas, have it create a prompt for Figma Make - his first instinct was that he didn't want to have another phone game.

So we created a game that mixed online game with real-world impact.

The game wasn't fully thought through - but the idea that you could sabotage other people's phones and make you interact in the real world for certain parts was fun - and made me excited about using phones together - vs feeling like every interaction is made worse with them.

I had the same thought - you can't ignore it -- but how do we make exposure to these tools mind opening vs limiting.
